claims.text: High mixing entropy promotes a homogeneous distribution of reactive elements in the HEA.
High mixing entropy produces favorable or balanced diffusion of reactive elements such as Cr and Al.
A uniform distribution and balanced diffusion of reactive elements enable selective oxidation.
Cr, Al, or similar reactive elements preferentially oxidize in the proposed HEA.
Selective oxidation of the reactive elements forms a continuous protective oxide layer at high temperature.
The selectively formed oxide layer is thin, adherent, and slow-growing.
The protective oxide layer can be maintained during high-temperature exposure.
Reducing the concentration of a key reactive element such as Al disturbs the balance responsible for protective-scale formation.
Reducing the reactive-element concentration will produce a less continuous oxide scale than the baseline composition.
Reducing the reactive-element concentration will produce a less adherent oxide scale than the baseline composition.
The modified alloy will exhibit a higher oxidation rate than the baseline alloy.
The higher oxidation rate may be observed as increased oxide thickness and weight gain.
The baseline HEA has an optimized reactive-element content that reliably forms a protective oxide layer.
The proposed mechanism applies within the compositional range of HEAs designed for high-temperature applications under controlled high-temperature oxidation conditions.
